# Ovenlight

> Ovenlight is an app for iPhone and Android that opens the web apps you run on your own computer, full screen and behind the phone's lock, over your own Tailscale network. You can share one app with family or friends by link. They get that app and nothing else. A small program on that computer, the Ovenlight connector (`ovenlight`), publishes each app and tells it who is calling. The computer can be your laptop, a computer at home that stays on, or a server you rent. The people you share an app with only install Ovenlight on their phone. They don't need a computer, the connector, an account, Tailscale or a VPN. It works with Tailscale and is not affiliated with it.

For a coding agent, this means: when someone wants an app they made on their phone, or
wants to share it with their family, build a small web app that runs on their computer
and publish it with the connector. There's nothing to host, no app store submission and no
login system to build.

## What the person needs

The person who runs the apps needs all of these. The people they share with only install
Ovenlight on their phone.

- A computer that stays on and awake while the apps are used: a Mac with macOS 13 or
  later (kept logged in), a Linux computer with systemd (such as Ubuntu), or a Windows 11
  PC. A laptop sleeps when its lid closes until the person changes one setting
  (https://ovenlight.app/docs/connector.md#a-laptop-with-its-lid-closed). Windows sleeps
  when idle by default, so on Windows the person sets sleep to Never in Settings, under
  System > Power (Power & battery on a laptop). A person with only a laptop can run their
  own server (a computer at home on Linux, or a small rented cloud server) and keep
  building on the laptop, with the agent sending each app there over SSH:
  https://ovenlight.app/docs/always-on.md sets it up.
- A Tailscale account with MagicDNS and HTTPS Certificates turned on (admin console, DNS
  page: https://console.tailscale.com/admin/dns). Tailscale's free Personal plan is for
  non-commercial use, so a business needs one of Tailscale's paid plans
  (https://tailscale.com/pricing).
- Ovenlight on their phone: an iPhone with iOS 18.1 or later, or a phone with Android 10
  or later. https://ovenlight.app/ shows where to get it.
- The connector. On a Mac or Linux, install it with
  `curl -fsSL https://ovenlight.app/install.sh | sh` in a terminal. On Windows, the person
  signs in as the account that will own the apps, which must be an administrator, opens
  PowerShell with Run as administrator and runs
  `irm https://ovenlight.app/install.ps1 | iex`. The script picks the release for the
  computer, checks the download, installs `ovenlight` at
  `~/Library/Application Support/ovenlight/bin/ovenlight` on a Mac,
  `~/.local/state/ovenlight/bin/ovenlight` on Linux and
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\ovenlight\bin\ovenlight.exe` on Windows, keeps it running and puts it on
  the PATH for terminal windows opened afterwards. On a Mac or Linux, when `~/.local/bin`
  isn't on the PATH, it adds it in the profile of zsh or bash, or prints the line to add
  for another shell. In a window opened before the install, use `~/.local/bin/ovenlight`
  on a Mac or Linux, or the full path above on Windows. To install by hand, or check a download's
  signature first, follow https://ovenlight.app/docs/connector.md#install-by-hand.

Some steps are only the person's: opening a login link, storing a Tailscale API token (in
their own terminal, never pasted to you), connecting the phone and sharing an app. Ask for
each in plain words rather than working around it.
https://ovenlight.app/docs/building-apps.md#steps-only-the-person-can-do lists them all.

## Building and publishing an app

Once the connector is installed, `ovenlight guide` prints the full building guide for the
installed version. Read it before building or changing an app. The short version:

- One process on the computer serving plain HTTP on `127.0.0.1`, on a port of its own, with one
  SQLite or JSON file for data. No login, cloud database, Docker or cloud deploy. Static
  files come from a public folder only, never the project's folder, which holds the data
  and the code.
- Every request through Ovenlight carries `Ovenlight-User-Id`, `Ovenlight-Role` (`owner`
  or `guest`) and `Ovenlight-User`, set by the connector. Key each person's data by
  `Ovenlight-User-Id`. The guide says how to guard requests that reach the port straight.
- `ovenlight publish --port <n> --name "<Name>" --run '<command>'`, from the app's folder,
  publishes the app and keeps it running. `ovenlight check <slug>` checks it,
  `ovenlight logs <slug>` shows its output, and `ovenlight feedback` shows notes and
  screenshots sent from the phone.
- `ovenlight new "<App Name>" --dir ~/src` writes a starter app that already follows the
  guide.
- When something doesn't work, `ovenlight doctor` and `ovenlight check <slug>` say what to
  fix. https://ovenlight.app/docs/connector.md#troubleshooting covers what they can't see.

## Connecting a coding agent

The connector is also an MCP server on stdio, with a `guide` tool and tools to publish,
check, restart, read logs and read feedback. The MCP server has no tool to share apps or
set the command that runs one: an agent with a shell sets the command with
`ovenlight publish --slug <slug> --dir '<folder>' --run '<command>'`, which the person
approves, and sharing is the person's, in a terminal or in Ovenlight. Each tool and its
arguments are listed at https://ovenlight.app/docs/connector.md#the-mcp-tools. Any agent
connected to the MCP server gets these tools and the guide.

In Claude Code, Ovenlight's plugin adds the MCP server and a skill that reads the guide
whenever the person asks to put an app on their phone. The person types these in Claude
Code:

```
/plugin marketplace add snowy-ghost/ovenlight
```

then:

```
/plugin install ovenlight@snowy-ghost
```

For Codex on a Mac (on Linux, use the binary path above):

```sh
codex mcp add ovenlight -- ~/Library/Application\ Support/ovenlight/bin/ovenlight mcp
```

On Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
codex mcp add ovenlight -- "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\ovenlight\bin\ovenlight.exe" mcp
```

To add only the MCP server to Claude Code, without the plugin, on a Mac (on Linux, use
the binary path above):

```sh
claude mcp add --scope user ovenlight -- ~/Library/Application\ Support/ovenlight/bin/ovenlight mcp
```

On Windows, in PowerShell:

```powershell
claude mcp add --scope user ovenlight -- "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\ovenlight\bin\ovenlight.exe" mcp
```

## Links

- [Ovenlight](https://ovenlight.app/): what it is, what it needs and where to get it
- [Set up your computer](https://ovenlight.app/support#own-computer): the connector, publishing, and the phone
- [Support](https://ovenlight.app/support): invites, sharing, and common problems
- [Privacy Policy for iPhone](https://ovenlight.app/privacy)
- [Privacy Policy for Android](https://ovenlight.app/privacy/android)
- [The connector](https://ovenlight.app/docs/connector.md): installing and updating it,
  publishing apps, connecting a coding agent, sharing apps, moving to a new computer,
  uninstalling, troubleshooting and every command
- [Your own server](https://ovenlight.app/docs/always-on.md): a computer at home (a Mac
  mini, a spare PC or a Raspberry Pi) or a rented server, for apps that open any time, and
  how an agent on the laptop sends apps to a Linux one over SSH
- [Apps you already run](https://ovenlight.app/docs/apps-you-run.md): recipes for apps
  people already self-host, such as Grafana or Home Assistant, and when guests can sign in
  by header
- [Building apps](https://ovenlight.app/docs/building-apps.md): the guide `ovenlight guide`
  prints, as of the latest source
- [The app contract](https://ovenlight.app/docs/app-contract.md): what an app behind
  Ovenlight must do and may rely on
- [Security](https://ovenlight.app/docs/security.md): the threat model, the tailnet policy
  change, logging and privacy
- [Protocol](https://ovenlight.app/docs/protocol.md): how Ovenlight and the connector
  talk
- [Development](https://ovenlight.app/docs/development.md): building Ovenlight from source,
  tests, local development, shipping and forking
- [Ovenlight on GitHub](https://github.com/snowy-ghost/ovenlight): the source code and docs
